As the gaming industry focuses heavily on upcoming major releases, players seeking variety this holiday season have several recent titles to consider. While blockbuster momentum often dominates headlines, a packed release calendar offers distinct alternatives for those looking to explore different genres.

Notable Releases and Revivals

Recent months have seen publishers launch major titles across multiple platforms. Among the highlighted games are several franchise revivals and arcade-style experiences designed to appeal to specific player preferences.

  • Onimusha: Way of the Sword (Capcom): Marking a return for the franchise, this title places players in the role of historical swordsman Miyamoto Musashi in a dark, Edo-era Kyoto. It features challenging swordplay and boss encounters, with mechanics compared to titles like Sekiro: Shadows Die Twice and Elden Ring, alongside a more accessible difficulty setting for story-focused players.
  • Star Wars: Galactic Racer (Fuse Games): Functioning as a spiritual successor to classic arcade racers and 1999's Star Wars Episode 1: Racer, this title emphasizes high-speed, aggressive racing. It includes modern roguelike elements in its tournament mode, allowing players to upgrade landspeeders and speeder bikes with handling-altering perks.
  • Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve (Bandai Namco): Returning the arcade flight simulator genre to the spotlight, this entry combines dogfighting action with a narrative involving geopolitics and pilot perspectives. Players operate modern and futuristic jets against large-scale targets, offering a spectacle-driven experience distinct from traditional simulators.

Practical Implications and Reader Verification

For readers evaluating holiday purchases, understanding what is confirmed versus what remains subjective is essential.

  • Confirmed Facts: The featured games—Onimusha: Way of the Sword, Star Wars: Galactic Racer, and Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve—represent notable releases discussed in recent industry roundups and video features.
  • Uncertainties: Individual enjoyment of difficulty curves, control schemes, and narrative styles varies widely by player.
  • How to Verify: Readers can review official publisher websites, platform storefronts, and critical consensus aggregators to check platform compatibility, pricing, and specific gameplay features before making a purchase.

For the complete discussion and additional alternative recommendations, readers can review the original coverage at [CNET](https://www.cnet.com/tech/gaming/the-best-games-that-arent-gta-6-this-holiday-season/).
